issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only changes the starting points of SLSQP: random uniform starts become scrambled Halton points (bases 2 and 3). There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and the code does not depend on the test inputs.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The Halton points are shifted by rng.uniform and reordered by rng.permutation, so all randomness still comes from the seed. The points are scaled into [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], just as before. The existing repair step and the harness's exact validity check are unchanged. The added cost is O(n log n) for n=32, which is negligible.

Recomputed z from the numbers above: the difference is 2.9396 - 2.9366 = 0.0030 in favour of the candidate. With sd 0.0034, SE = 0.0034*sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00416, so z ≈ 0.72. This matches the reported 0.713; the small gap is likely from rounding the inputs. Reject is the right provisional decision at z ≈ 0.7, since a 0.003 gain is within the noise.

Note: the candidate's single run (2.9396) is above the 'best published' 2.9370 stated on the card. A packing that passes the harness check cannot be invalid, so this most likely means the card's reference value is out of date (sums near 2.9395 have been reported for n=32). Even so, it is the only figure above the stated best and comes from 1 run, so a replicate would be worth it before relying on it.
The candidate has only 1 run against 2 for the incumbent. If this idea is still wanted, replicate it to get more statistical power before deciding.
